rationale: This is the level-to-change restatement of the already-tested "Operating Margin Trade Credit Coverage" (and overlaps heavily with "Gross Margin Current Asset Discipline" and "Margin Turnover Improvement Confirmation"), i.e. a cosmetic first-difference variant rather than a new mechanism.

target_name: Cash Cycle Weak Link Margin Trap
rationale: The MAX "weakest-link" aggregation is a genuinely different functional form from the archive's SUMRANK cash-cycle composites and the sign logic of the MUL construct is internally consistent, though the two legs are mechanically correlated so MAX may add little beyond the average.

target_name: Debt Funded Working Capital Profit Trap
rationale: It joins two previously tested legs (short-term-debt funding and noncash current-asset buildup) into a conjunctive funding-gap story that plausibly diagnoses why the debt-funded trap had a weak alpha, though it is incremental and mixes at- and sale-scaled inputs inside the SUMRANK.

This is "Net Profit Self Funded Cash Cover" with the profitability leg swapped from ni/at to oiadp/sale and the cash leg rescaled by sales — a cosmetic re-scaling of an already-evaluated signal with no new economic content.

The second leg is the (monotone) reciprocal of the archived "Operating Margin Trade Credit Coverage" liability-coverage leg and the first leg is the archive's standard MA gross-margin block, so this is a recombination of two tested components rather than a new test.

Count-based persistence of working-capital discipline is a defensible new angle distinct from the archive's single-period flow legs, but the 0–5 discrete leg will create massive ties that dominate the MIN and the 5-year window will shrink coverage, so temper expectations for the portfolio leg.
